Jared / Anya —

Per our kickoff today, attaching the evaluation plan (short) and proposing the MAP timeline for the performance work you asked for. Goal: prove our hosted endpoint meets your latency and TTFT targets at both burst and sustained traffic patterns and identify any queueing/rate-limit interactions before contract sign.

High level test matrix (attached PDF has details):
- Burst window: 3000 concurrent sessions for 30s and sustained 800 concurrent for 30m
- Targets: p95 latency <= 450ms for 512-token prompts, TTFT < 80ms, throughput up to 120 requests/sec sustained
- Variants: quantized model v1 (fast), fp16 model (quality baseline)
- Observability: token-level latency, queue length, kernel utilization, and per-route error rates

Next steps:
1) Acme to confirm peak concurrency profile and acceptable burst duration (Jared) — by Tue 11/16
2) Redwood to run initial burst vs sustain probe in our U.S. region and share raw CSV + analysis — target end 11/18
3) Joint review and tuning session (30m) to adjust rate-limit windows and warm-up concurrency the week of 11/22

I attached eval-plan-v2.pdf with the detailed schedule and the CSV schema we'll deliver. I'll coordinate with Neha and Marissa on the test execution.

Subject: RE: Mutual action plan: performance evaluation & surge vs sustain testing — probe results & recommendations

Jared / Anya —

Thanks for the joint run today. Summary of the runs (attached CSV has raw samples):

Burst probe (quantized-v1):
- Peak concurrency reached: 3,120
- Observed p95 latency (512 tokens): 420ms
- Median TTFT: 68ms; p95 TTFT: 92ms
- Sustained tokens/sec during hold period: ~9800 tokens/sec total
- Max observed queue length: 610 requests (spike lasted ~18s)
- Rate-limit behavior: with a hard 429 threshold configured at 150 req/s we saw immediate 429s once global windows saturated; with token-bucket soft policy (refill 100 req/1.5s per route) we observed graceful beta-backoff and no dropped connections

Sustain probe (fp16 baseline):
- Target sustained concurrency: 820 average over 120m
- p95 latency: 530ms (degraded under heat)
- TTFT median: 110ms (higher mixing due to kernel thrash)
- Observed throughput: steady ~118 req/s

Key findings and recommendations:
1) Quantized-v1 meets p95 latency and TTFT targets under burst when token-bucket soft throttling is used — recommend defaulting to quantized-v1 for your release traffic and fall back to fp16 for high-quality paths.
2) Queueing observed during the burst exceeded 500 requests for ~18s — increase the burst window to 45s in the MAP if you want to fully characterize rebalancing and pre-warm capacity for release events.
3) Rate-limit policy: recommend soft token-bucket per-route with refill tuned to 100–150 req/1.5s and a global circuit-breaker that sends informative Retry-After headers. That gives graceful degradation instead of abrupt 429 storms.
4) Warm-up: add a 60s warm-up where we pre-warm KV cache and issue low-priority synthetic requests to minimize kernel thrash during first few seconds of a spike.
5) Follow-up run: schedule a 45s burst with a wider warm-up and collect the kernel traces; propose Wed 11/24 09:00 PST.

Next deliverables: surge-vs-sustain-results.csv (attached) and a 1-page exec summary I'll circulate once Marissa and Laura review.

If this looks good, I'll include the recommended rate-limit config as a JSON snippet in the exec summary for procurement.

Thanks,
Karthik
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
